title: The breakthrough
tagline: Two pawns die so one can queen

principles.prompt: Three pawns abreast on your 5th rank face three at home, kings far away. What's possible?
principles.answer: A forced passed pawn with no king help: the middle pawn sacrifices itself — twice over — and one outside pawn walks through.

principles.prompt: What's the move-order rule for the breakthrough?
principles.answer: Middle pawn first. If they capture toward the a-side, push the c-pawn; toward the c-side, push the a-pawn. The surviving outside pawn is past every defender.

principles.prompt: The enemy trio faces yours and it's your move. What kills their breakthrough forever?
principles.answer: The same push, made first — advancing your middle pawn one square denies the sacrifice forever. Prophylaxis costs one tempo and saves the game.

principles.prompt: You're spending two pawns to promote one. What must you count first?
principles.answer: That your queen arrives before their counterplay: the breakthrough takes three moves plus the pawn's run, and the new queen must be in time to hunt down whatever they got moving meanwhile.

demos.title: b6 and the walls come down
demos.intro: No kings needed. Watch three home pawns lose to three on the fifth — by force.

steps.note: The middle pawn walks into two captures. Both lose.
— so the c-pawn steps past. It attacks b7 and cannot be ignored.
And the a-pawn is through: nothing stands between it and a8. Two pawns spent, one unstoppable.
Black's survivors run too — this is the race you counted before playing b6.
Queened, two full tempi ahead. From a8 the queen hunts the runners down from behind. Count first, then sacrifice.

tests.title: Middle pawn first
tests.intro: Kings out of play, trios facing. There is exactly one way through — and one move order.

wrong.a6: bxa6 bxa6 and your pawns are corked — a-file blocked, nothing runs. The breakthrough starts with the middle pawn.
wrong.c6: bxc6 bxc6 and everything locks — the breakthrough starts with the middle pawn, not a wing.
wrong.Kf2: The window is one move wide — bring the king over and Black's king arrives too, covering the queening squares.

hints: Only one pawn attacks two defenders at once.
b6 — whichever way Black captures, push the other wing pawn through the hole.

tests.explanationAfter: Middle pawn first: axb6 was met by c6, bxc6 by a6, and the a-pawn is past every defender with two tempi to spare. Had Black taken the other way — cxb6 — the mirror works: a6, then c6. One order, two symmetric endings.

tests.title: Southbound crash
tests.intro: Your trio on the fourth, theirs at home. Same demolition, other direction.

wrong.h3: gxh3 gxh3 and the h-file corks itself — middle pawn first, always.
wrong.f3: gxf3 gxf3 and everything locks — the middle pawn is the battering ram, not the wings.
wrong.Kc7: One tempo of king-play and White's king starts back — the breakthrough window closes.

hints: The mirror of the drill you just did: which of your pawns attacks two defenders?
g3 — after hxg3, f3 rips the next hole; after gxf3, h3 walks through.

tests.explanationAfter: The g-pawn bought the file, the f-pawn bought the follow-up, and the h-pawn runs to h1 with White's king a spectator. Breakthroughs are colour-blind — learn the shape, not the side.
